_what: Known two-party Democratic vote share within demographic groups, used to reweight the sample before fitting. See scripts/fit_models.py, rake_to_targets().
_why: The CES reads under-30 voters as roughly 11 points more Democratic than they voted in 2024, and trending the wrong way since 2016. That is a wrong vote rate WITHIN the group, so reweighting the age composition cannot fix it - only a target for the group's vote can.
_how_to_fill: Each entry is: cycle -> feature -> level -> the group's vote.
Enter it as {"dem": 55, "rep": 42} straight off the exit-poll table. The two-party conversion is done for you; do not do it by hand.
A bare fraction between 0 and 1 is also accepted if you have already normalised.
Use an independent measurement, not an impression. The national exit poll (Edison / NEP) age crosstab is the usual source; AP VoteCast is an alternative from 2018 on.
Record where each number came from in _sources. A target with no citation is a prior wearing a data costume, and this file exists to keep those apart.
Leave a cycle out entirely rather than guessing at it. The fit skips cycles with no targets and says so.
Valid age levels: 18_29, 30_44, 45_64, 65_up. The fit fails loudly on any other name.
